title: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM, VARIANT TYPE
alt_titles: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM WITH NORMAL DNA REPAIR RATES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that the variant type of xeroderma pigmentosum (XPV) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH; also called hRAD30).

checks.claim: The variant type of xeroderma pigmentosum (XPV) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH).
checks.evidence_quote: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract links XPV to POLH mutations but does not say whether they are homozygous or compound heterozygous.

checks.claim: POLH is also called hRAD30.
checks.evidence_quote: harbor nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30, the human counterpart of yeast RAD30
checks.explanation: The paper uses the name hRAD30. Giving the approved symbol POLH alongside it is a standard nomenclature restatement.

paragraphs.text: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XPV) is an inherited disorder with clinical photosensitivity and a higher rate of sunlight-induced skin cancer. Unlike cells from the excision-repair-deficient forms of xeroderma pigmentosum (groups XP-A to XP-G), XPV cells carry out normal nucleotide excision repair. However, they cannot replicate ultraviolet (UV)-damaged DNA normally (Masutani et al., 1999; Itoh et al., 2000).

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XPV) is an inherited disorder with clinical photosensitivity.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant show clinical photosensitivity, skin neoplasias induced by ultraviolet light, and defective postreplication repair, but normal nucleotide excision repair.
checks.explanation: Photosensitivity is stated directly. The abstract groups XPV among 'hereditary photosensitive disorders', which covers 'inherited'.

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XPV) is associated with a higher rate of sunlight-induced skin cancer.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is an inherited disorder which is associated with increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.

checks.claim: XPV cells carry out normal nucleotide excision repair, unlike cells from the excision-repair-deficient xeroderma pigmentosum groups XP-A to XP-G.
checks.evidence_quote: Unlike other xeroderma pigmentosum cells (belonging to groups XP-A to XP-G), XP-V cells carry out normal nucleotide-excision repair processes

checks.claim: XPV cells cannot replicate UV-damaged DNA normally.
checks.evidence_quote: but are defective in their replication of ultraviolet-damaged DNA.

paragraphs.text: The term 'pigmented xerodermoid' had been used for a condition whose mild clinical symptoms suggested it was similar to, but distinct from, xeroderma pigmentosum. Cleaver et al. (1980) found that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture could not be distinguished from XP variant cells in UV-irradiated assays of unscheduled DNA synthesis, strand breakage during repair, chain growth during semiconservative replication with or without caffeine, and recovery of DNA replication. They concluded that the term 'pigmented xerodermoid' was redundant.

checks.claim: The term 'pigmented xerodermoid' had been used for a condition with mild clinical symptoms suggesting it was similar to, but distinct from, xeroderma pigmentosum.
checks.evidence_quote: The "pigmented xerodermoid" was previously defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms that suggested it might be similar to but distinct from xeroderma pigmentosum (XP).
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Cleaver et al. (1980) found that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture could not be distinguished from XP variant cells in UV-irradiated assays of unscheduled DNA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: irradiated with ultraviolet light and unscheduled DNA synthesis, strand breakage during repair, chain growth during semiconservative DNA replication with or without caffeine, and the recovery of DNA replication were determined. It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant
checks.explanation: Unscheduled DNA synthesis is one of the assays listed, and the paper concludes overall that the cells are indistinguishable. The abstract does not give results for each assay separately.

checks.evidence_quote: irradiated with ultraviolet light and unscheduled DNA synthesis, strand breakage during repair, chain growth during semiconservative DNA replication with or without caffeine, and the recovery of DNA replication were determined. It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant
checks.explanation: Strand breakage during repair is one of the assays listed, and the paper concludes overall that the cells are indistinguishable.

checks.evidence_quote: chain growth during semiconservative DNA replication with or without caffeine, and the recovery of DNA replication were determined. It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant
checks.explanation: Chain growth during semiconservative replication, with or without caffeine, is one of the assays listed, and the paper concludes overall that the cells are indistinguishable.

checks.claim: Cleaver et al. (1980) found that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture could not be distinguished from XP variant cells in UV-irradiated assays of recovery of DNA replication.
checks.evidence_quote: and the recovery of DNA replication were determined. It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant
checks.explanation: Recovery of DNA replication is one of the assays listed, and the paper concludes overall that the cells are indistinguishable.

checks.evidence_quote: It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant and the former term is therefore redundant.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Cleaver (1972) described variants of xeroderma pigmentosum that had normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.

checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum: variants with normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
checks.explanation: The title says directly that the XP variants had normal DNA repair.

checks.claim: Cleaver (1972) described variants of xeroderma pigmentosum that had normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum: variants with normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
checks.explanation: The title says directly that the XP variants had normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.

paragraphs.text: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that cells from the class of XP patients with normal excision repair handled DNA synthesis abnormally after UV irradiation. In these variant cells, low-molecular-weight DNA made after irradiation took much longer than in normal cells to convert to high-molecular-weight DNA. Caffeine strongly inhibited this slow conversion but had no effect in normal cells. Two excision-repair-defective XP cell lines showed intermediate effects in both respects.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that cells from XP patients with normal excision repair handled DNA synthesis abnormally after UV irradiation.
checks.evidence_quote: There is, however, one class of these patients whose cells are completely normal in this excision repair process. We have found that these cells have an abnormality in the manner in which DNA is synthesized after UV-irradiation.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In XP variant cells studied by Lehmann et al. (1975), low-molecular-weight DNA made after UV irradiation took much longer than in normal cells to convert to high-molecular-weight DNA.
checks.evidence_quote: The time taken to convert initially low-molecular-weight DNA synthesized in UV-irradiated cells into high-molecular-weight DNA similar in size to that in untreated cells is much greater in these variants than in normal cells.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that caffeine strongly inhibited the slow conversion of low- to high-molecular-weight DNA in UV-irradiated XP variant cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Furthermore, this slow conversion of low to high-molecular-weight newly synthesized DNA is drastically inhibited by caffeine, which has no effect in normal cells.
checks.explanation: 'Drastically inhibited' in the paper matches 'strongly inhibited' in the claim.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that caffeine had no effect on conversion of low- to high-molecular-weight DNA in UV-irradiated normal cells.
checks.evidence_quote: this slow conversion of low to high-molecular-weight newly synthesized DNA is drastically inhibited by caffeine, which has no effect in normal cells.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that 2 excision-repair-defective XP cell lines showed intermediate effects in both the delayed DNA conversion and caffeine inhibition.
checks.evidence_quote: Two cell lines from classes of xeroderma pigmentosum that are defective in excision-repair show intermediate effects, with regard to both the time taken to convert newly synthesized DNA to high molecular weight and the inhibition of this process by caffeine.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Cleaver et al. (1980) proposed that XP variant cells lack a gene product that lets normal cells replicate DNA without interruption at UV-induced pyrimidine dimers. Without it, replication forks are blocked more often and at lower doses.

checks.claim: Cleaver et al. (1980) proposed that XP variant cells lack a gene product that lets normal cells replicate DNA without interruption at UV-induced pyrimidine dimers.
checks.evidence_quote: The defect common to these cell types appears to be the loss of a gene product that permits normal cells to replicate DNA without interruption at damaged sites (u.v.-induced pyrimidine dimers).
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly; the authors frame it as what the defect "appears to be", which matches "proposed".

checks.claim: Cleaver et al. (1980) proposed that in XP variant cells, replication forks are blocked more often and at lower UV doses.
checks.evidence_quote: The consequence of this loss is that replication forks are blocked more frequently and at lower doses in XP variant cells.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly. The doses are the UV doses used in the experiments.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (1991) noted that XP variant cells are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to the cytotoxic effect of UV, but are significantly more sensitive to its mutagenic effect. They transfected an XP variant cell line with a UV-irradiated shuttle vector carrying the supF gene. Mutant frequency rose linearly with dose, with a slope 5 times steeper than in normal cells. Of 53 independent mutants, 52 had base substitutions, and 62 of 64 substitutions involved a dipyrimidine. Twenty-eight percent of mutations involved A:T base pairs, compared with 11% in normal cells. The authors suggested that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to insert dAMP opposite bases involved in photoproducts.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (1991) noted that XP variant cells are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to the cytotoxic effect of UV.
checks.evidence_quote: are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to the cytotoxic effect of UV radiation
checks.explanation: The abstract states this as background.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (1991) noted that XP variant cells are significantly more sensitive than normal cells to the mutagenic effect of UV.
checks.evidence_quote: However, they are significantly more sensitive to its mutagenic effect.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (1991) transfected an XP variant cell line with a UV-irradiated shuttle vector carrying the supF gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we transfected an XP variant cell line with a UV-irradiated (at 254 nm) shuttle vector carrying the supF gene as a target for mutations
checks.explanation: The abstract describes exactly this experiment.

checks.claim: In the XP variant cell line studied by Wang et al. (1991), supF mutant frequency rose linearly with UV dose, with a slope 5 times steeper than in normal cells.
checks.evidence_quote: The frequency of mutants increased linearly with dose, but with a slope 5 times steeper than that seen with normal cells.
checks.explanation: The linear dose response and the 5-fold steeper slope both match the abstract.

checks.claim: Of 53 independent supF mutants from XP variant cells studied by Wang et al. (1991), 52 had base substitutions.
checks.evidence_quote: 52 of 53 independent mutants generated in the XP variant cells contained base substitutions
checks.explanation: The counts match the abstract.

checks.claim: Of 64 base substitutions in supF mutants from XP variant cells studied by Wang et al. (1991), 62 involved a dipyrimidine.
checks.evidence_quote: with 62 of 64 of the substitutions involving a dipyrimidine
checks.explanation: The counts match the abstract.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (1991) found that 28% of supF mutations in XP variant cells involved A:T base pairs, compared with 11% in normal cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Twenty-eight percent of the mutations involved A.T base pairs, with the majority found at position 136, the middle of a run of three A.T base pairs. (In the normal cells, this value was only 11%.)
checks.explanation: Both percentages match the abstract.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (1991) suggested that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to insert dAMP opposite bases involved in photoproducts.
checks.evidence_quote: If the rate of excision of lesions from supF in the two cell lines is equal, our data suggest that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to incorporate dAMP opposite bases involved in photo-products.
checks.explanation: The authors make this suggestion, though only on the condition that both cell lines remove lesions at the same rate. The draft's 'suggested' is close enough.

paragraphs.text: Using DNA combing, Despras et al. (2010) found that in UV-irradiated XPV cells, the translesion synthesis defect sharply reduced the number of active replication forks and left a high proportion of forks stalled. Irradiated XPV cells formed extensive regions of single-strand DNA during replication, which over-activated the ATR/Chk1 pathway after low UVC doses. Adding a low concentration of caffeine after irradiation reduced Chk1 activation and abolished DNA synthesis in XPV cells. Inhibiting Chk1 with UCN-01 worsened fork stalling and sensitized XPV cells to UVC, as caffeine does. The authors concluded that polymerase eta acts at stalled forks to restart their progression. In its absence, Chk1 becomes essential for resuming replication by alternative pathways through fork stabilization.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) used DNA combing to study UV-irradiated XPV cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Using DNA combing, we showed that translesion synthesis defect leads to a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks
checks.explanation: The abstract describes using DNA combing to study replication in UV-irradiated XP-V cells.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that in UV-irradiated XPV cells, the translesion synthesis defect sharply reduced the number of active replication forks.
checks.evidence_quote: translesion synthesis defect leads to a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks in human cells
checks.explanation: The abstract states this reduction in active forks directly.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that in UV-irradiated XPV cells, a high proportion of replication forks were stalled.
checks.evidence_quote: a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks in human cells
checks.explanation: The abstract states that a high proportion of forks were stalled.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that irradiated XPV cells formed extensive regions of single-strand DNA during replication.
checks.evidence_quote: extensive regions of single-strand DNA are formed during replication in irradiated XP-V cells
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that in XPV cells, the ATR/Chk1 pathway was over-activated after low UVC doses.
checks.evidence_quote: leading to an over-activation of ATR/Chk1 pathway after low UVC doses
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that adding a low concentration of caffeine after irradiation reduced Chk1 activation in XPV cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Addition of a low concentration of caffeine post-irradiation, although inefficient to restore S-phase progression, significantly decreases Chk1 activation and abrogates DNA synthesis in XP-V cells.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that post-irradiation caffeine decreased Chk1 activation.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that adding a low concentration of caffeine after irradiation abolished DNA synthesis in XPV cells.
checks.evidence_quote: significantly decreases Chk1 activation and abrogates DNA synthesis in XP-V cells
checks.explanation: 'Abrogates' is the same as 'abolished'.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that inhibiting Chk1 with UCN-01 worsened replication fork stalling in XPV cells.
checks.evidence_quote: it aggravates replication defect in XP-V cells by increasing fork stalling
checks.explanation: The abstract states that UCN-01 worsened the replication defect by increasing fork stalling.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) found that inhibiting Chk1 with UCN-01 sensitized XPV cells to UVC, as caffeine does.
checks.evidence_quote: Consequently, UCN-01 sensitizes XP-V cells to UVC as caffeine does.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) concluded that polymerase eta acts at stalled replication forks to restart their progression.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings indicate that poleta acts at stalled forks to resume their progression
checks.explanation: 'Restart their progression' means the same as 'resume their progression'.

checks.claim: Despras et al. (2010) concluded that in the absence of polymerase eta, Chk1 becomes essential for resuming replication by alternative pathways through fork stabilization.
checks.evidence_quote: In the absence of poleta, Chk1 kinase becomes essential for replication resumption by alternative pathways, via fork stabilization.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion directly.

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (2000) identified compound heterozygous mutations in a patient with XPV, each inherited from a heterozygous parent. This is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) identified compound heterozygous mutations in a patient with XPV.
checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations.
checks.explanation: The patient carries two different heterozygous mutations inherited from the parents, which is compound heterozygosity.

checks.claim: In the XPV patient studied by Itoh et al. (2000), each mutation was inherited from a heterozygous parent.
checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations.
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms inheritance of each mutation and refers to the parents as heterozygotic.

checks.claim: The inheritance pattern in the XPV family studied by Itoh et al. (2000) is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells from heterozygotic parents showed normal levels of unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis
checks.explanation: Unaffected heterozygous parents and an affected compound heterozygous child fit recessive inheritance, but the abstract never says 'autosomal recessive'.

paragraphs.text: Masutani et al. (1999) isolated from HeLa cells a DNA polymerase that bypasses UV-induced thymine dimers to continue replication on damaged DNA in XPV cell extracts. They identified it as the human homolog of yeast Rad30, DNA polymerase eta. All XPV cells they examined carried mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene. Recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrected the inability of XPV cell extracts to replicate past thymine dimers on damaged DNA.

checks.claim: Masutani et al. (1999) isolated from HeLa cells a DNA polymerase that bypasses UV-induced thymine dimers to continue replication on damaged DNA in XPV cell extracts.
checks.evidence_quote: we have recently isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that continues replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers in XP-V cell extracts.

checks.claim: Masutani et al. (1999) identified the thymine-dimer-bypassing polymerase as the human homolog of yeast Rad30, DNA polymerase eta.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that this polymerase is a human homologue of the yeast Rad30 protein, recently identified as DNA polymerase eta.

checks.claim: Masutani et al. (1999) found that all XPV cells they examined carried mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.

checks.claim: Masutani et al. (1999) found that recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrected the inability of XPV cell extracts to replicate past thymine dimers on damaged DNA.
checks.evidence_quote: Recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrects the inability of XP-V cell extracts to carry out DNA replication by bypassing thymine dimers on damaged DNA.

checks.evidence_quote: Here it is shown that XP variant (XP-V) cell lines harbor nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30

checks.claim: hRAD30 is the human counterpart of yeast RAD30.
checks.evidence_quote: hRAD30, the human counterpart of yeast RAD30
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Johnson et al. (1999) identified 8 hRAD30 mutations in XPV cell lines.
checks.evidence_quote: Of the eight mutations identified, seven would result in a severely truncated hRad30 protein.
checks.explanation: The abstract says eight mutations were identified.

checks.claim: Of the 8 hRAD30 mutations identified by Johnson et al. (1999), 7 were predicted to produce a severely truncated hRad30 protein.
checks.evidence_quote: Of the eight mutations identified, seven would result in a severely truncated hRad30 protein.
checks.explanation: The paper's 'would result in' matches the draft's 'predicted to produce'.

paragraphs.text: In a Japanese family with XPV, Itoh et al. (2000) found that the patient carried 2 heterozygous missense mutations in the POLH gene, each inherited from a parent. One was an A-to-G transition at nucleotide 1840 causing a lys535-to-glu (K535E) substitution. The other was an A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 affecting lys589. Neither mutation was found in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) studied a Japanese family with XPV.
checks.evidence_quote: Each of these mutations were absent in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
checks.explanation: That the family is Japanese is only implied by the choice of Japanese controls; it is not stated outright.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) found that the XPV patient in a Japanese family carried 2 heterozygous missense mutations in the POLH gene.
checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations.
checks.explanation: The two heterozygous missense mutations are stated, but the abstract does not name POLH.

checks.claim: In the Japanese XPV patient studied by Itoh et al. (2000), each POLH missense mutation was inherited from a parent.
checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations.
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms that each mutation was inherited.

checks.claim: One POLH mutation found by Itoh et al. (2000) in a Japanese XPV patient was an A-to-G transition at nucleotide 1840 causing a lys535-to-glu (K535E) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: One mutation is an A-->G transition at nucleotide 1840 that generates a K535E mis-sense mutation.
checks.explanation: Nucleotide position, base change and amino acid change all match.

checks.claim: One POLH mutation found by Itoh et al. (2000) in a Japanese XPV patient was an A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 affecting lys589.
checks.evidence_quote: Another mutation is an A-->C transversion at nucleotide 2003 that generates a K589 mis-sense mutation.
checks.explanation: Nucleotide position, base change and affected residue all match.

checks.claim: Neither the POLH K535E mutation nor the POLH nucleotide 2003 A-to-C mutation was found in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: Each of these mutations were absent in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
checks.explanation: Stated directly, with the same control count.

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (1996) described a simple autoradiographic method for diagnosing XPV. Patient fibroblasts and normal control cells were plated side by side and tested for 3 markers after UV irradiation: unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis. Among the hereditary photosensitive disorders tested, which included xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome, only XPV cells showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis and normal RNA synthesis recovery together with reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (approximately 50% of control). Caffeine increased this reduction.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (1996) described a simple autoradiographic method for diagnosing XPV.
checks.evidence_quote: We present here an alternative simple method for the diagnosis of xeroderma pigmentosum variant that measures three cellular markers for DNA repair by autoradiography
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a simple autoradiographic method for diagnosing XPV.

checks.claim: In the autoradiographic method of Itoh et al. (1996), patient fibroblasts and normal control cells were plated side by side.
checks.evidence_quote: Fibroblasts from a patient are plated on three coverslips parallel with normal cells (control).
checks.explanation: Patient and normal cells are plated in parallel and compared with adjacent normal cells, which matches 'side by side'.

checks.claim: In the method of Itoh et al. (1996), cells were tested after UV irradiation for unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after ultraviolet irradiation
checks.explanation: The abstract names all three markers, measured after UV irradiation.

checks.claim: The hereditary photosensitive disorders tested by Itoh et al. (1996) included xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Of the hereditary photosensitive disorders including xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome, and newly established ultraviolet-sensitive syndrome
checks.explanation: The abstract lists the same three disorders.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (1996) found that, among the hereditary photosensitive disorders tested, only XPV cells showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis and normal RNA synthesis recovery together with reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibit normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis
checks.explanation: The abstract states this marker pattern directly.

checks.evidence_quote: reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (approximately 50% of that of control cells)
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the same figure of about 50% of control.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (1996) found that caffeine increased the reduction in recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in XPV cells.
checks.evidence_quote: This reduction of DNA synthesis is enhanced in the presence of caffeine.
checks.explanation: The abstract says caffeine enhances the reduction.

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (2000) found that recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in XPV cells was 51 +/- 6% of normal controls and fell to 36 +/- 5% with a nontoxic level of caffeine. They studied 2 families, each with a photosensitive patient identified as having XPV. Cells from the heterozygous parents had normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis. With 1 mM caffeine, however, their recovery of replicative DNA synthesis was reduced (53 +/- 8% of normal control). In colony-forming assays, the heterozygous cells survived UV normally without caffeine but slightly less well with 1 mM caffeine. The authors suggested that XPV heterozygotes can be identified by their UV sensitivity in the presence of nontoxic caffeine.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) found that recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in XPV cells was 51 +/- 6% of normal controls.
checks.evidence_quote: only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibited normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (51 +/- 6% the rate relative to normal controls)
checks.explanation: The 51 +/- 6% figure matches.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) found that recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in XPV cells fell to 36 +/- 5% of normal controls with a nontoxic level of caffeine.
checks.evidence_quote: This reduction of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis was enhanced in the presence of a nontoxic level of caffeine to 36 +/- 5%.
checks.explanation: The 36 +/- 5% figure with nontoxic caffeine matches.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) studied 2 families, each with a photosensitive patient identified as having XPV.
checks.evidence_quote: In this study we assess the cellular markers in two independent families that included two photosensitive patients that were identified as xeroderma pigmentosum variant.
checks.explanation: Two families with two photosensitive XPV patients, as claimed.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) found that cells from heterozygous parents of XPV patients had normal unscheduled DNA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells from heterozygotic parents showed normal levels of unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis
checks.explanation: Normal unscheduled DNA synthesis is stated.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) found that cells from heterozygous parents of XPV patients had normal recovery of RNA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells from heterozygotic parents showed normal levels of unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis
checks.explanation: Normal recovery of RNA synthesis is stated.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) found that cells from heterozygous parents of XPV patients had normal recovery of replicative DNA synthesis without caffeine.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells from heterozygotic parents showed normal levels of unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis, but reduced rates of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in the presence of 1 mM caffeine
checks.explanation: Recovery was normal without caffeine and reduced only with caffeine.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) found that with 1 mM caffeine, recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in cells from heterozygous parents of XPV patients was reduced to 53 +/- 8% of normal control.
checks.evidence_quote: reduced rates of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in the presence of 1 mM caffeine (53 +/- 8% relative to the normal control)
checks.explanation: The 53 +/- 8% figure with 1 mM caffeine matches.

checks.claim: In colony-forming assays by Itoh et al. (2000), cells heterozygous for XPV survived UV normally without caffeine.
checks.evidence_quote: with a colony-forming assay, the cells showed normal survival by ultraviolet without caffeine
checks.explanation: Normal UV survival without caffeine is stated.

checks.claim: In colony-forming assays by Itoh et al. (2000), cells heterozygous for XPV survived UV slightly less well with 1 mM caffeine.
checks.evidence_quote: but slightly reduced survival by ultraviolet with 1 mM caffeine present
checks.explanation: Slightly reduced UV survival with 1 mM caffeine is stated.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) suggested that XPV heterozygotes can be identified by their UV sensitivity in the presence of nontoxic caffeine.
checks.evidence_quote: These results suggest that xeroderma pigmentosum variant heterozygotes can be identified by their sensitivity to ultraviolet irradiation in the presence of nontoxic levels of caffeine.
checks.explanation: The authors' conclusion matches the claim.

paragraphs.text: In a Japanese patient with xeroderma pigmentosum variant type (XPV), Itoh et al. (2000) found compound heterozygosity for 2 missense mutations in the POLH gene. One was an A-to-G transition at nucleotide 1840 causing a lys535-to-glu (K535E) substitution. The other was an A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 affecting lys589. Each mutation was inherited from a heterozygous parent and was absent from 52 unrelated Japanese individuals. Cells from the heterozygous parents showed reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after UV irradiation in the presence of 1 mM caffeine.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) found compound heterozygosity for 2 missense mutations in the POLH gene in a Japanese patient with XPV.
checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations.
checks.explanation: Two inherited heterozygous missense mutations are stated, but the abstract does not name POLH and only implies the patient is Japanese (through the Japanese controls).

checks.claim: One POLH mutation in the Japanese XPV patient studied by Itoh et al. (2000) was an A-to-G transition at nucleotide 1840 causing a lys535-to-glu (K535E) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: One mutation is an A-->G transition at nucleotide 1840 that generates a K535E mis-sense mutation.
checks.explanation: Nucleotide position, base change and amino acid change all match.

checks.claim: One POLH mutation in the Japanese XPV patient studied by Itoh et al. (2000) was an A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 affecting lys589.
checks.evidence_quote: Another mutation is an A-->C transversion at nucleotide 2003 that generates a K589 mis-sense mutation.
checks.explanation: Nucleotide position, base change and affected residue all match.

checks.claim: In the Japanese XPV patient studied by Itoh et al. (2000), each POLH mutation (K535E and the nucleotide 2003 A-to-C mutation) was inherited from a heterozygous parent.
checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations.
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms inheritance of both mutations, and the parents are described as heterozygotic.

checks.claim: The POLH K535E mutation and the POLH nucleotide 2003 A-to-C mutation were absent from 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: Each of these mutations were absent in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
checks.explanation: Stated directly, with the same control count.

checks.claim: Cells from the heterozygous parents of the Japanese XPV patient with POLH K535E showed reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after UV irradiation in the presence of 1 mM caffeine.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells from heterozygotic parents showed normal levels of unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis, but reduced rates of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in the presence of 1 mM caffeine
checks.explanation: Reduced recovery with 1 mM caffeine is reported for the heterozygous parents in both families.

paragraphs.text: For discussion of the A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 of the POLH gene, which affects lys589 and was found in compound heterozygous state in a Japanese patient with XPV, see the K535E mutation (Itoh et al., 2000).

checks.claim: The A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 of the POLH gene affects lys589.
checks.evidence_quote: Another mutation is an A-->C transversion at nucleotide 2003 that generates a K589 mis-sense mutation.
checks.explanation: The nucleotide 2003 A-to-C change affecting lys589 matches.

checks.claim: The POLH nucleotide 2003 A-to-C transversion was found in compound heterozygous state, together with the POLH K535E mutation, in a Japanese patient with XPV.
checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations. One mutation is an A-->G transition at nucleotide 1840 that generates a K535E mis-sense mutation. Another mutation is an A-->C transversion
checks.explanation: Co-occurrence with K535E in a compound heterozygous state is supported, but the abstract does not name POLH and only implies the patient is Japanese.
